sections.h2: Which sale route is fastest in Brookhaven
sections.html:
Pace varies by route. An as-is buyer with cash can set the closing day with you, whereas a listing waits on showings, an appraisal and the buyer's mortgage. The money at stake is large. The 2020 to 2024 midpoint for a Brookhaven owner-occupied house is $692,700, about twice the $332,700 U.S. figure, so one percentage point of price is a lot of dollars.

  • Full listing: strongest exposure, plus staging, repair lists and the lender's calendar.
  • Owner-handled sale: no commission to pay, but buyers, contracts and disclosures are yours to manage.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer steps and no repair demands, normally at a figure below a polished listing.

The sections below cover what is particular to Brookhaven: housing numbers, permit rules, code enforcement and the DeKalb County tax process.

sections.h2: A young city in DeKalb County
sections.html:
Brookhaven incorporated in December 2012, and its police department opened for service on July 31, 2013. It covers 11.69 square miles of land and runs 19 parks, three swimming pools, two recreation centers and a community building on 352 acres of parkland.

Water and sewer come from DeKalb County, and DeKalb's watershed department staffs a 24-hour emergency line at 770-270-6243. Rules on short-term rentals, building permits and construction hours come from the city's own code, so check Brookhaven's pages, not the county's, when you plan work on a house here.

Brookhaven had 59,643 residents in mid-2025, 5.1 percent above the April 2020 estimates base, living in 24,271 households that average 2.36 people.

Every figure covers the whole city, so one house may sit far off the midpoint. Buyers and tenants here come from a wide mix of backgrounds, and a listing with clear photos and plain, specific details reaches all of them.

Brookhaven allows short-term rentals only for a resident owner holding a permit. Council adopted the Short-Term Rental Ordinance on April 23, 2019, and each permitted house may be rented no more than 180 days per year.

  • The applicant must have owned the property for over a year and hold a current DeKalb homestead exemption.
  • No permit goes to a business entity such as an LLC, a partnership or a family trust.
  • One owner, one permit, and permits are limited to five percent of residential parcels in each council district.
  • The permit costs $25 for one year and renews annually.

The permit ends when the property changes hands, so a buyer who wants a rental starts a fresh application. For permits that predate October 24, 2023, a new owner has six months after title transfer to apply without being turned away on the district cap. Ask Community Development how your council district stands before you pitch the house to investors.

sections.h2: Permits and work hours when preparing to sell
sections.html:
Construction or redevelopment of any kind needs a city permit from the Community Development Department. Contractors present a Georgia license, while a homeowner working on their own house can sign a notarized Homeowner Affidavit.

Wait 10 business days for review before calling about status. The city's fee schedule lists the minimum and review fees, which use the ICC data valuation table. Complaints about work outside permitted hours go to police through 911. Allowed hours are 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday and 8 am to 5 pm on Saturday, with no work on Sunday. You can also report construction without a permit, and tree removal without one, through the Brookhaven Connect app. Close out permits on finished work before a buyer's inspector asks about it.

DeKalb County, not the city, appraises Brookhaven homes. Its appraisal department sets taxable value at fair market value times 40 percent. If you dispute the value, the recorded property features or a homestead denial, you have 45 days from the notice date to appeal.

Three appeal paths exist. The Board of Equalization costs nothing and uses a three-member panel. A hearing officer is available at no filing fee for non-homestead property over $500,000. Non-binding arbitration needs a certified appraisal at the owner's expense and a $217 filing fee. File online with the access code printed on the notice, or mail the appeal to 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

The share of the DeKalb homestead exemption you receive depends on when you file.

  • January 1 to April 1: 100.00% of the exemption.
  • April 2 to April 30: 66.67%.
  • May 1 to May 31: 58.33%.
  • June 1 to June 30: 50.00%.

Ask the DeKalb tax commissioner what remains due on the current bill so the amount can be divided at closing. A buyer who sees a reduced exemption on the bill will ask why, and the filing date is usually the answer. If you are selling soon after buying, check that your own application went in before April 2.

Neighbors can report problems through the Brookhaven Connect app, and the list reads like a pre-listing checklist: tall grass or vegetation, trash or outside storage, inoperable vehicles, illegal dumping, graffiti, construction without a permit and tree removal without a permit. A house with an open complaint can slow a buyer's lender or surprise a cash buyer, so walk the lot and clear these items first.

Police dispatch runs through ChatComm, so 911 doubles as the non-emergency line. The city's parcel and land-use maps can help you check zoning and boundaries before you list. Ask Community Development about any open permit or violation on your address. Unresolved items are far easier to clear before a contract than after. A cash buyer will often take a house with a few open items, but the price will reflect the work, so a clean record helps in either kind of sale.

DeKalb County will not record your deed until Georgia's transfer tax is settled. The sale is reported on Form PT-61, filed electronically through the clerks' portal. The tax is $1 up to the first $1,000 of price, then 10 cents for every additional $100 or part of $100, and the seller is liable unless the contract says differently.

For a ruling on whether a particular deed is exempt, ask the county clerk. Filing trouble goes to the portal's support line at 800-304-5174, and whoever runs your closing normally files the form.

faqs.a: No. It incorporated in December 2012, and its police department began work on July 31, 2013, so Brookhaven counts among Georgia's youngest cities.

faqs.q: What is the midpoint home value in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: $692,700 for owner-occupied homes in the 2020 to 2024 data. Your house may price above or below that figure.

faqs.q: Will a new buyer inherit my short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. The permit ends when ownership changes. Permits go only to owner-occupants with a DeKalb homestead exemption who have owned the property for more than a year.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute a DeKalb value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. Use the access code on the notice to file online, or mail the appeal to DeKalb County Property Appraisal, 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

faqs.q: Who pays Georgia's transfer tax at a Brookhaven closing?
faqs.a: The seller, by default, and a contract can move it to the buyer. It is paid ahead of recording, with PT-61 filed online.
